text_read: repaired digest plus full source checked for Aramaic-only passages: Vaera 2, Vayera 4 (Sitrei Torah), Bereshit 7 para 6 (I:18b), Yitro 1 para 49 (II:69a), Bereshit 66 paras 15-18 (I:42a-43a, not in digest; read in source lines 337-341)
mode_evidence: The text locates the vision in the physical eye: 'close thine eye and press thine eyeball', 'radiating and luminous colours which can only be seen with closed eyes', seen in the rolling or turning of the eye. The open eye sees the non-luminous mirror; the closed eye sees the luminous one. The Soncino editor reads the colours as not attached to any material background.
onset_evidence: A one-line instruction with no prerequisites: close the eye and turn/roll the eyeball (Aramaic satim einakh ve-ascher galgalakh; Soncino 'press'), and shining colours appear that are given only to closed eyes. Sitrei Torah grades three ways of seeing, the third a shining mirror seen only in the rolling of the fully shut eye, which cannot be held. Bereshit 66 para 17 states the dependence physiologically: were it not for the eye's visible colours, the shining colours would not appear when the eye is shut and rolled. No time scale, no training. Practice or figure: the text treats it as a real, repeatable act that the reader is told to perform, but always as a demonstration ('ve-raza da', 'this mystery') of the relation of revealed to hidden Sefirot, never as a cultivated contemplative regimen; Bereshit 66 uses it explicitly as a simile ('like that sight seen in closing when the eye rolls'). Full seeing of the higher colours remains Moses's alone.

conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: eye shut, eyeball pressed or rolled
conditions.other: Balaam looked at the light with a 'closed eye' and saw a small light as through a wall

stages.label: three colours at a distance, narrowed, and in the rolling of the shut eye
stages.description: Sitrei Torah: the third is a mirror of light seen only in the closed rolling eye; one cannot stay in that colour.

stages.label: non-luminous vs luminous mirror
stages.description: The open eye sees the lightless mirror (seeing); the closed eye sees the luminous mirror (knowing).

stages.label: sparkling radiance in the rolled closed eye (zahara natzitz)
stages.description: Bereshit 66 para 16: the contents of the palaces are like the sight seen in closing when the eye rolls, where a sparkling radiance appears; what is not seen in that rolling is the spirit ruling over all.

what_to_do_with_light: Use the visible colours as a means to apprehend the hidden ones; the Patriarchs knew the concealed colours through the revealed ones. The vision cannot be held, per Sitrei Torah.
obstacles_and_fixes: The luminous colour cannot be kept in view (Sitrei Torah).
cautions: Balaam saw only a thin streak of light through the husk, knowing not what he said; the vision is not trustworthy when the seer is impure.
Only Moses beheld the highest colours.
interpretation: The closed-and-rolled-eye colours are a physical demonstration of the luminous mirror above the visible, non-luminous colours; the Zohar uses this real effect as the model for the hidden Sefirot, for the radiance hidden in the pupil (I:18b), and for the linked palaces of prayer (I:42a-43a).
practice_summary: The Zohar's instruction is brief: close the eye and press or turn the eyeball, and radiant, shining colours appear that cannot be seen with open eyes. A parallel text distinguishes three ways of seeing: from afar with the eye narrowed, with the eye nearly shut and opened a little, and a radiance seen only in the rolling of the fully closed eye, which the seer cannot hold steady. The open eye shows only the lightless mirror. The visible colours, white, red and green in the bow, serve as a way to infer the hidden luminous ones. No preparation, duration or troubleshooting is given. Balaam's looking with a 'closed eye' shows the same method with a flawed seer.
